Definition: an ephah or measure for grain; hence, a measure in general
BiblicalUsage: ʼêyphâh is a plain word for an ephah or measure for grain; hence, a measure in general. In Exodus 16:36, the text says "Now an omer [is] the tenth [part] of an ephah." In Leviticus 5:11, the text says "then he that sinned shall bring for his offering the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a sin offering."
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simple: ʼêyphâh tells me that worship is not a performance but a response — we answer what God has done with what we are. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
